articles.title_orig: ‘Maxi merde’: French presidential campaign rattled by a week of chaos
articles.title_zh: ‘Maxi merde’: French presidential campaign rattled by a week of chaos
articles.content_orig:
PARIS — French schools are getting torched. The far right’s brightest star is fighting for his political life after being accused of antisemitic remarks. And economic indicators are flashing bright red to warn of a potential sovereign debt disaster in the country.
The crises that have rocked France in recent days are exacerbating partisan cleavages in the country’s increasingly no-holds-barred presidential campaign.
In the words of one government adviser: “It’s the maxi merde .”
Though that individual, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the current situation, was only referring to the increasingly violent demonstrations outside secondary schools and the government’s slow-footed response to them, it’s a sentiment likely shared by French voters after a week of particularly bleak headlines.
If there are political winners, it’s not immediately clear who they are. Establishment candidates and moderate voices are still struggling to seize the narrative from far-right presidential front-runner Marine Le Pen and her surging far-left challenger Jean-Luc Mélenchon — both of whom want to fundamentally reshape France and its relationship with Europe.
A survey by pollster Odoxa this week found that the French disapprove of the government’s handling of the student school protests, but they also disapprove of Mélenchon and his far-left party France Unbowed’s involvement.
Mélenchon’s allies have joined demonstrators outside schools, saying they were there to show support and protect minors from confrontations with police. But the government and France Unbowed’s political opponents accuse them of fanning the flames of violence — allegations they deny.
“There’s a battle over the narrative” between the political extremes, a Socialist Party adviser said.
Whatever the case, the week’s crises are showing just how nasty the campaign can get with two populist candidates unafraid to stoke partisan divisions leading the polls.
The French government has tried to get a grip on the unravelling protests, holding a crisis meeting Thursday and meeting youth representatives on Friday.
“Lecornu is always running behind the crises, he’s always reacting,” said a centrist adviser.
Le Pen, however, blamed agitators for stirring up violence at the protests and accused France Unbowed of “giving a helping hand” to “agents of chaos and insurrection.”
For her National Rally party, the crisis is a useful opportunity to try to convince voters that her party is the best choice for those concerned with public safety.
“We have a government that is incapable of maintaining public order and a left that is stoking the fire,” said National Rally MP Laurent Jacobelli in an interview with POLITICO.
“We are the only legitimate ones when it comes to [security],” he added.
But the unrest is also a useful distraction for Le Pen as her party president and heir apparent, Jordan Bardella, tries to bat down allegations published Monday by investigative outlet Mediapart that he sent antisemitic messages on Facebook Messenger when he was a 17-year-old activist.
Bardella vehemently denied the allegations and vowed to sue Mediapart, but the website on Thursday published another story outlining how it verified the claims, which included screenshots and conversation data downloaded directly from Meta with the help of their sources.
Bardella was tipped to become Le Pen’s prime minister if she came to power, but his future appears to hang on a thread.
“Do we need to unplug him? It’s Marine’s decision,” said a National Rally elected representative. “It all depends on whether the proof is serious.”
But Bardella is no small player, and the National Rally’s opponents are hoping that the fallout of his possible resignation would damage Le Pen’s campaign durably.
All of this comes just hours after Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s minority government introduced a 2027 budget with €43 billion worth of savings designed to reassure markets fretting about France’s massive debt and a stubbornly high budget deficit.
But without a parliamentary majority, getting lawmakers to agree to painful cuts will be tough, even if the specter of a potential financial crisis is starting to loom large.
Borrowing cost have reached their highest levels since 2008 and the spread between French 10-year bonds and German ones — an indicator that measures investors’ appetite to hold French debt over more traditionally stable German debt — shot above 150 basis points on Friday, a level not seen in years.
One lawmaker from President Emmanuel Macron’s party Renaissance said he doesn’t see how the presidential hopefuls from the political center — former PMs Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal — will be spared the fallout.
“Every minute spent on the budget is a minute spent staring at our incapacity to get ourselves out of the mess,” the MP said.
Meanwhile, Mélenchon has called for his party officials to join more protests planned next Tuesday and protect pupils against alleged police violence. That could propel him to center stage, but it could also backfire if he is seen as taking part in the unrest.
Centrist MEP Sandro Gozi said the allegations against Bardella and the far left’s attitude to the protests “complicate the normalization strategy of the two sides.”
“Both Le Pen and Mélenchon are extremists who are far from fundamental Republican and European values,” Gozi said.
But as Macron’s term winds down, a sense is taking hold that France has been mismanaged and that parts of the country are falling apart.
It’s a perception any would-be successor with links to the current president will struggle to combat on the campaign trail.
Elisa Bertholomey and Sarah Paillou contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Gemini app gains new ‘Map’ tool, replacing ‘/’ with ‘@’
articles.title_zh: Gemini app gains new ‘Map’ tool, replacing ‘/’ with ‘@’
articles.content_orig:
Google has introduced a “Map” tool to aid your location-based Gemini app prompts on Android and iOS. Meanwhile, the Gemini app is already getting ready to replace the forward slash for skills.
On mobile (not available on the web), you can find “Map” at the end of the carousel alongside Photos, Camera, Avatar, Files, Drive, and Notebooks.
This launches a live map of your current location with a circular focus area. You can pan and zoom in/out as needed, while the magnifying glass icon in the top-right corner lets you search for any location. Once you’ve made a selection, hit “Explore this area.”
This adds “Map Area” to the prompt box where you can append text. The Map tool is widely rolled out.
With the latest Google app beta (version 17.63), Gemini is replacing the forward slash (“/”) to invoke skills with the “@” symbol that’s already used for Connected Apps, which will soon be renamed to “Connectors.”
Google just announced on Wednesday that skills will replace Gems and that you can use a slash in the prompt box to activate. We’re seeing the following prompt when entering a slash:
/ is now @. Access your skills, connectors and more from a single place.
The box that appears is slightly wider than before, with skills appearing first and a shortcut to create new ones. This change is not widely rolled out yet.

articles.title_orig: Cornell 'gang rape' case: Hochul, Letitia James give update after AG appointed special prosecutor
articles.title_zh: Cornell 'gang rape' case: Hochul, Letitia James give update after AG appointed special prosecutor
articles.content_orig:
NEW YORK (WABC) -- The Cornell rape accuser was "failed" by people obligated to protect her, including police and the prosecutor, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said at a news conference on Friday.
A visibly outraged Hochul blasted Cornell University Police, the Tompkins County district attorney and the state's rape laws before introducing Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the controversial case
James told a packed news conference at the governor's office that this is now "an active criminal investigation." She pledged a full and fair investigation.
"Every New Yorker deserves to know that when they report a crime, it will be investigated fully and fairly, that they will be seen and heard, that is the promise of our justice system," James said.
Hochul said the system failed Jane Doe. Information from her interview with police was not passed to the district attorney, who then failed to interview her.
"I am deeply disturbed by Cornell University's police and how they handled this," Hochul said. She said sending a "partial record" to the district attorney was a failure.
"In what world would the police learn from the victim that she had literally been gang raped" and that she believed "100%" she had been raped and not elevate those allegations, Hochul said.
Hochul claimed the Tompkins County district attorney then did not do the "bare minimum" and interview the woman after receiving the six-page police report.
"In what world does the district attorney not interview her or even request the full transcript?" Hochul asked again. That is "exactly why we're here today and why I took the action last night ."
Tompkins County District Attorney Matt Van Houten told ABC News that CUPD's six-page summary of Jane Doe's allegations convinced him no crime occurred.
Hochul also took the opportunity to call for a change in the state law around voluntary intoxication in cases of sexual assault. She said lawmakers must address this part of the law as soon as possible.
Jane Doe's attorney said he and his client are "pleased" the governor appointed a special prosecutor because "contradictions between the district attorney's statements and those of the Cornell police have been shocking."
Van Houten said Friday he supports the governor's decision to remove him from the case and pledged his cooperation with the attorney general.
Cornell has also endorsed Hochul's decision to remove the DA from the case and assign it to James.
"We fully support the appointment of a special prosecutor and efforts to change New York State's rape law and are committed to an independent external review of all aspects of how Cornell has handled this case," a spokesperson said.

articles.title_orig: Stocks rise after soft jobs data; Nasdaq hits record led by Nvidia: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stocks rise after soft jobs data; Nasdaq hits record led by Nvidia: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stocks rose Friday following a surprisingly weak jobs report that raised hopes the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in October.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 250 points, or 0.5%. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.2%, hitting an all-time high earlier in the day before pulling back as Treasury yields reversed course.
Despite Friday's rally, the Dow was down for the week by about 1.3%. The S&P was little changed, off 0.3%, while the Nasdaq was up 0.6% on the week, with Friday marking its third straight advance.
Treasury yields initially fell Friday following the September employment report, but later rebounded, pushing U.S. equities off their highs for the session.
Tech stocks rallied as risk-taking returned on Wall Street, with shares of Nvidia hitting an all-time high for the first time since May, though it closed below its previous record close. CrowdStrike , Palo Alto Networks and AMD also all rose to all-time highs. Shares of AMD also rose nearly 3%.
Last month's nonfarm payrolls report showed the U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs last month, with unemployment rising to 4.2%. The Dow Jones consensus called for jobs growth of 84,000 and for the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.1%.
"This is the exact kind of number the market wanted from a labor standpoint," said Phil Blancato, chief market strategist at Osaic. "Not too hot, not too cold ... not overly great, and not weakening."
That number made traders reassess the next move for the Federal Reserve. Fed funds futures trading suggests a 77% likelihood the central bank will stand pat at this month's meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
Saira Malik, chief investment officer at Nuveen, told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the report may give the market support before earnings season kicks off, which she thinks will be "very strong."
"So, I think this could be the start of the Santa Claus rally that we've all been hoping for," she said.
Oil prices pulled back , supporting equities, following a report that European nation states are considering a release of strategic fuel reserves following pressure from the Trump administration.
Investors are coming off a modestly higher session Thursday, to start off the month of October. However, the Dow and the S&P 500 were headed for weekly losses amid a global bond rout, while the Nasdaq was the only major average on pace to end the week with gains.
— CNBC's Jeff Cox contributed to this report
The three major averages rose on Friday following softer-than-expected jobs data.
The S&P 500 advanced 0.49% to 7,722.93. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.19% to end at 27,190.86, while the Dow Industrials rose 250.88 points, or 0.49%, to close at 51,177.44.
Friday's rally put the Nasdaq Composite on track for another winning week.
The technology-heavy index jumped more than 1% in Friday trading, bringing its weekly gain to 0.5%. If that holds, it would mark the Nasdaq's third positive week in a row.
The Nasdaq is the only major U.S. stock index on track to finish in the green. The Dow and S&P 500 have slid about 1.2% and 0.2%, respectively, in the period.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average on Friday was pacing to end the week in the red, despite Friday's 0.5% advance.
The blue-chip index as of late Friday trading was down more than 1% for the week. It's the Dow's fourth negative week in the last five, with its positive one in that time period coming last week when it finished up just under 0.3%.
Citi raised its price target on shares of bitcoin treasury firm Strategy to $240 per share from $136 per share, implying about 34% upside potential.
The change reflects a more bullish outlook for bitcoin over the next year and a higher valuation of Strategy's bitcoin holdings as a result, Citi analyst Peter Christiansen said in a note Friday.
The bank also maintained its buy rating on Strategy, though Christiansen noted investors should take a more cautious view of Strategy's valuation due to the company's growing but "dilutive" cash reserve, which could reduce the benefit of its bitcoin holdings.
Strategy shares were up 3% in early morning trading.
Nike shares fell 6% at the open after tanking 10% in the premarket after the global sportswear apparel giant delivered a mixed first quarter of fiscal 2027 that showed its turnaround timeline is further than expected.
The company reported weak trends in its key China market, despite growth in its core North America segment.
While Nike plans $2.5 billion in cost savings by 2031, management said it expects revenues to decline in the high single digits in 2027.
The stock is down 46% for the year.
October marks the fourth birthday of the global bull market, one where the future trajectory is still to the upside, according to UBS.
"Over the past four years, global stock markets have reached one record high after another because corporate earnings are growing faster than most analysts expected. What many initially interpreted as a short-term recovery has proved to be a structural upswing with global reach," Burkhard Varnholt, senior financial market adviser at UBS Switzerland, wrote Friday.
"We therefore see the real story of this bull market as less about prices and more about an economic revival," Varnholt added.
Tesla deliveries in the third quarter beat Wall Street's expectations on Friday, coming at 486,532 versus 461,100 expected.
Deliveries eased from 497,099 in the year-ago period but climbed up from the second quarter's 480,126 delivered vehicles.
Shares were up in morning trading on Friday.
The Grayscale Zcash ETF (ZCSH) is up more than 60% in the past month, bringing its year-to-date gain to about 253%, thanks to renewed interest in privacy as speculative capital this year has rotated into AI.
Zcash (ZEC) itself – up more than 170% this year compared to bitcoin , which is stagnant on the year – was designed to keep users' financial transactions completely private. It launched in 2016, but the privacy narrative eventually faded as privacy coins became a compliance headache for regulators and exchanges.
Crypto's mainstream investment case has become increasingly institutionalized and transparent, while AI has made large-scale financial surveillance and transaction analysis more powerful. The combination of the two has allowed the privacy narrative to gain traction and lead to the launch of the Grayscale Zcash ETF in August.
By comparison, the popular iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) is down about 1% this year and the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF (BITW) , which tracks the 10 largest cryptocurrencies, is down 5%. Meanwhile, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF has gained 12% and the Invesco QQQ is up nearly 22%.
Nvidia popped on Friday, briefly hitting an all-time intraday high.
Shares of the semiconductor firm rose more than 3% to as much as $237.88 on the day. At its peak, the stock traded at its highest intraday level ever.
Nvidia's shares began trading on the public market in January 1999.
Revisions in the September jobs report for July and August are making those months look weaker for job creation.
July was marked down by 31,000 to mark a net job loss of 10,000 on the month, the Labor Department reported Friday. August was marked down by 29,000 for a new total of 133,000 compared to the initial robust report of 162,000.
"Revisions made both July and August look weaker, too. Over the past 3 months, we've an average of a mere +17k per month," economist Justin Wolfers wrote on social media .
Stocks opened higher Friday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 322 points, or 0.6%. The S&P 500 gained 0.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.1%.
The latest fed funds futures trading showed an 86% likelihood that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady when it convenes for its Oct. 27-28 meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. That's up from a roughly 76% chance just one day prior.

articles.title_orig: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
articles.title_zh: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
articles.content_orig:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn".
The woman, known as Jane Doe in legal documents, alleges she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024.
The case was investigated at the time but no charges were laid. It recently reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight.
At a news conference on Friday, Hochul said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled. She has now appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead the case.
This appointment was made after Hochul said she "lost faith" in the local prosecutor's ability to oversee the investigation.
Expressing outrage that local prosecutors did not interview the accuser themselves,  Hochul on Friday said: "This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her."
She has also vowed to close a "loophole" that prevents prosecutors from pursuing rape charges in cases when the victim has voluntarily consumed drugs or alcohol. Jane Doe is believed to have voluntarily taken drugs and alcohol on the night of the alleged gang rape.
"If someone is too intoxicated to consent it should not matter if they chose to use drugs or alcohol," said Hochul, adding: "Voluntary intoxication is not a licence for gang rape."
James, who is the state's chief legal officer, appeared alongside Hochul at Friday's news conference, pledging to "lead a process guided by the facts and the law".
She said her office would interview witnesses and pursue prosecutions if warranted.
District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who previously led the investigation, has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.
Van Houten said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office.
In a statement on Friday, he said he supported James' investigation, adding: "It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the university."
Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.
Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September.
Speaking to CNN on Friday, her lawyer Thomas Giuffra said she is "not doing well".
"She's under siege on social media, where people are trying to identify her; some false court postings, attempting to identify her," he said.
Survivor and victim advocates say current state law on sexual assault makes it difficult for charges to be brought against perpetrators if the victim voluntarily took drugs or drank alcohol before the alleged assault took place.
A bill to address what Hochul described as a legal loophole was already before the state legislature prior to this week's public outcry over how police and investigators handled the Cornell rape allegations.
People who have voluntarily become intoxicated to the point that they are unable to give consent are currently not protected by New York's rape laws, says state assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz, who first sponsored legislation to close the loophole in 2019.
"The real bottom line is that right now if you are voluntarily intoxicated, you will not get justice," he tells BBC News.
"Being voluntarily intoxicated, basically, is almost like giving somebody a get out of jail free card."
Dinowitz says that around half of US states have already changed their laws to say it makes no difference whether intoxication is voluntarily or involuntarily in rape cases.
Hochul said she will support the existing bill and that it could move forward as early as the next legislative session which reconvenes in January. As governor, she could also call lawmakers back for a special session before then.

articles.title_orig: Spain's government dealt blow after parliament rejects housing measures. Early election speculated
articles.title_zh: Spain's government dealt blow after parliament rejects housing measures. Early election speculated
articles.content_orig:
Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez that increases pressure on him to call a snap election.
Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by the government in response to nationwide protests that have followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, from her home.
The decrees, which introduced a series of initiatives aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market, required parliamentary approval in order to remain in place.
MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.
Hundreds of demonstrators had gathered outside Congress as the debate took place and there were angry scenes.
Protesters chanted "shame on you" and "your profits, our misery", after the results were announced.
The government's defeat underlines the fact that Sánchez, a Socialist, does not command a congressional majority and it has heightened speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.
Sources told Spanish media that the government would spend the weekend deciding its next step, and whether to dissolve parliament.
Sánchez's beleaguered government had already been mired in a series of scandals and judicial cases affecting his Socialist Party and close allies.
Abascal was evicted after she was unable to pay a sharp rent increase introduced by Urbagestión, the company that owned her flat in central Madrid.
Hundreds of protesters gathered to oppose the eviction last week and the case triggered a broader movement across the country demanding affordable rentals, which have soared in recent years.
The social backlash has seen Urbagestión negotiate the return of Abascal to her flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued, with people occupying squares in Madrid and other cities, pitching tents in squares and with a series of marches scheduled for this weekend.
The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".
Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.
The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.
The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".
The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas .
The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.
However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.
Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress.
"I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," Sánchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary".
He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".
Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms.
"Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said.
"Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."
However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour.
She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happening… these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."
The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.
Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

articles.title_orig: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.title_zh: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.content_orig:
U.S. District Court Judge James Boasberg, who blocked President Donald Trump from deporting hundreds of Venezuelan migrants, is among the judges who have attracted attention from critics. 'Fox News @ Night' takes a closer look.
An Obama-appointed judge blocked President Donald Trump from firing court-appointed U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington Roger Rogoff, ordering the Justice Department to recognize Rogoff as the rightful officeholder and restore his ability to serve.
"This is yet another ruling from an activist judge trying to thwart President Trump’s agenda and undermine his constitutional authority. U.S. attorneys serve at the pleasure of the President," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.
Judge Stanley Bastian, who was first nominated by Obama in 2013, issued a preliminary injunction reinstating Rogoff and barring the administration from treating him as having been lawfully removed. The ruling sets up a legal fight over whether a president can fire a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges. A 1979 Justice Department opinion and a 2000 federal appeals court ruling both concluded that the president has that authority.
"We disagree with the decision and intend to seek an immediate stay and will appeal," the DOJ Rapid Response account wrote.
TRUMP ADMIN FIRES US ATTORNEY IN SEATTLE MINUTES AFTER HE WAS APPOINTED
President Donald Trump’s administration secured an interim Supreme Court victory allowing it to continue third-country deportations while the legal battle plays out. (Getty Images)
Some legal experts and conservative attorneys took to social media to sharply criticize the ruling, arguing it infringes on the president's constitutional authority over the executive branch.
"Another lawless and dangerous ruling. Violating the separation of powers. By another Democrat activist judge. This time? Seattle Obama Judge Stanley Bastian," wrote Article III founder and president Mike Davis .
"Democrat judges handpicked their own U.S. attorney. The President, through his attorney general, fired him. Under Article II of the Constitution , the President clearly has the executive power to fire Justice Department officials," Davis added.
Davis also noted Bastian’s first name was misspelled in the order, missing the "e" in Stanley.
'ROGUE' OBAMA JUDGE'S SMACKDOWN OF TRUMP ELECTION RULES PROVOKES OMINOUS WARNING FROM WHITE HOUSE DEPUTY
FILE - The majority of the cuts were aimed at Health and Human Services programs. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
"The Federal Judge misspelled his own name in his order. That's how you know it's quality legal work," wrote one user.
"Now Judge Bastian created an unnecessary constitutional crisis by essentially ordering a coup at the Justice Department, by ordering the removal of the President’s pick and putting in Bastian’s judicial puppet. The Ninth Circuit must fix this. Or the Supreme Court will have to step in. Again," Davis concluded.
"The President's power to remove U.S. Attorneys must be unfettered consistent with Article II of the Constitution. Judge Stanley Bastian is wrong here to order Rogoff reinstated. I predict Judge Bastian will eventually be reversed, whether at the Ninth Circuit or by the Supreme Court," said Oversight Project litigation vice president Jeff Clark .
WHITE HOUSE RIPS ‘ACTIVIST’ BIDEN JUDGE WHO UPENDED TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP ORDER
Justice Department lawyers asked a federal judge Friday to dismiss a lawsuit challenging the Anti-Weaponization Fund, arguing Attorney General Todd Blanche formally terminated it Aug. 2. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
"Judicial overreach, plain and simple. The judiciary does not get to run the Executive Branch. Period," said Holtzman Vogel partner Brian Nieves .
In Myers v. United States (1926), which centered on President Woodrow Wilson's firing of a postmaster without Senate consent, the Supreme Court ruled that the president generally has constitutional authority to remove executive branch officers.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
More recently, the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel concluded in a 1979 opinion that the president’s statutory authority to remove "each United States attorney" also extends to prosecutors appointed by federal judges.
The case is the latest in a string of legal fights over President Trump's U.S. attorney appointments, following similar disputes in New Jersey, Virginia and New York.
A similar dispute unfolded in New Jersey after the administration sought to keep Alina Habba leading the U.S. attorney’s office after her interim term ended. Federal courts ultimately rejected the administration’s effort to maintain her authority, although the judges’ original appointee, Desiree Grace, did not simply take over the office.
Rogoff’s case goes a step further, directly testing whether a president can remove a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges under the statutory process for filling a vacancy.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

Southern California is about to experience at least a week of extreme heat, according to the National Weather Service.
An extreme heat advisory is in effect for many areas from 10 a.m. Friday through 8 p.m. Thursday and may be extended. People are advised to remain hydrated, avoid the sun, stay in an air-conditioned room and check on loved ones.
A strong high-pressure system will set up over the eastern Pacific and West Coast starting Friday and will increase through Sunday, sending temperatures 15 to 20 degrees above normal, the weather service said.
That means when the Dodgers and Atlanta Braves take the field Saturday for the National League Division Series, it could be as hot as 95 degrees on the field.

Downtown Los Angeles is expected to reach highs of 99 to 103 degrees, warmer valleys between 102 and 107 degrees, and coastal areas from Santa Barbara to Los Angeles could reach 90 to 98 degrees over the weekend, the weather service forecast states.
Temperatures could climb higher Wednesday into Friday, potentially breaking daily records.
However, tropical moisture is expected to enter the area by next weekend, which could lead to some cooling, according to the weather service.
Meanwhile, a swell from Hurricane Rachel is expected to bring elevated surf of 5 to 6 feet to area beaches on Tuesday through Thursday, according to the weather service forecast.
The state’s coastlines have been inundated with high surf for much of the summer, leading to severe erosion at some of the state’s most popular beaches.

articles.title_orig: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.title_zh: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.content_orig:
Long-term data reinforce durable efficacy and safety of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in late-onset Pompe disease
BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc . (Nasdaq: BMRN ) today announced new data evaluating the efficacy and safety of POMBILITI® (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + OPFOLDA® (miglustat) in late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) were presented at the 31st Annual Congress of the World Muscle Society (WMS), in Hiroshima, Japan.
These results from the PROPEL open-label extension (OLE) study of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, which were shared in a late-breaking presentation, demonstrated durable motor function outcomes and relative stabilization of pulmonary function over long-term follow-up. The analysis included data from 82 individuals who received POMBILITI + OPFOLDA continuously from baseline observed in the initial PROPEL study (PROPEL baseline) to year five. For the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)-experienced cohort, the mean duration of prior ERT at baseline was 7.6 years. These data represent long-term benefits for people with LOPD followed in the study, including both ERT-experienced and ERT-naïve cohorts.
"These five-year results demonstrate that POMBILITI and OPFOLDA can provide durable, long-term benefits for people living with late-onset Pompe disease, including those who had been on enzyme replacement therapy for years before enrolling in the study," said Greg Friberg, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Research & Development Officer at BioMarin. "Sustaining motor function and limiting pulmonary decline for up to five years in a progressive disease like LOPD is clinically meaningful, and we remain committed to continuing to share long-term evidence to inform the care of people with this rare genetic condition."
Table 1. Efficacy Measures With POMBILITI + OPFOLDA From PROPEL Baseline (BL) for up to Five Years
Mean (standard deviation, SD) change from baseline in % predicted six-minute walk distance (pp6MWD)
Mean (SD) change from baseline in % predicted forced vital capacity (ppFVC)
No new safety signals were identified. 51.2% of participants (n=42) experienced treatment-related adverse events, the majority of which were manageable. Five individuals discontinued treatment for safety reasons, including two due to serious treatment-related adverse events (chills and hypoxia [n=1], anaphylactoid reaction [n=1]).
Phase 1/2 Data Show Positive Dystrophin Expression and Favorable Tolerability With Nivudirsen (BMN 351)
Additional presentations at WMS included data evaluating nivudirsen (BMN 351), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide for ambulatory boys ages 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. Included in these presentations was an update from the ongoing Phase 1/2 351-201 study, which was previously shared at the 19th International Congress on Neuromuscular Diseases in July. Results from 351-201 showed treatment with nivudirsen was generally well tolerated and led to consistently positive outcomes across multiple measures of therapeutic benefit, including expression of near full-length dystrophin.
Below are key presentations at WMS, with all times listed in Japan Standard Time:
Phase 1/2 Results of BMN 351, an Antisense Oligonucleotide for Exon 51 Skip-Amenable Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Poster Presentation #2.66P Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Comprehensive Panel of Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic and Biomarker Measures Drives Clinical Development of BMN 351 for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy E-Poster Presentation #2.43eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Muscle Composition and Muscle Injury Biomarkers Improve With BMN 351 Treatment E-Poster Presentation #2.59eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Five-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline E-Poster Presentation #3.081LBeP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Four-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline Poster Presentation #3.56P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Baseline Disease Burden and Real-World Monitoring Practices: Global Insights From the followME Pompe Journey Registry Poster Presentation #3.57P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
ATB200-03/07 Danish Subpopulation: Four-Year Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease E-Poster Presentation #3.35eP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
About the PROPEL Open-Label Extension Study
The Phase 3 open-label extension (OLE) study (ATB200-07; NCT04138277 ) is a multicenter, international study designed to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in adults with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) who completed the Phase 3 PROPEL study (ATB200-03; NCT03729362 ). Of the 118 people treated in the OLE, 82 continued POMBILITI + OPFOLDA treatment from PROPEL (62 ERT-experienced prior to PROPEL; 20 ERT-naïve) and 37 switched from the comparator arm to POMBILITI + OPFOLDA (29 ERT-experienced; eight ERT-naïve).
The study evaluates long-term changes from PROPEL baseline in six-minute walk distance (6MWD, the primary endpoint in PROPEL), forced vital capacity (FVC), creatine kinase (CK) and hexose tetrasaccharide (Hex4) levels, and patient-reported outcomes, as well as long-term safety.
The 351-201 trial ( NCT06280209 ) is a Phase 1/2 multicenter open-label dose-escalation study evaluating BMN 351 for the treatment of boys aged 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy with a specific genetic change amenable to exon 51 skipping. The primary endpoints examine the safety and tolerability of BMN 351, the secondary endpoints assess plasma, urine and muscle pharmacokinetics, and key exploratory endpoints include exon-skipping efficiency, dystrophin expression, immunogenicity and functional assessments.
The study is being conducted in three cohorts, with Cohort 1 being divided into Cohort 1A and Cohort 1B. In Cohort 1A, three boys received increasing doses once every two weeks with a visit to assess safety measures collected the week after dosing prior to escalating doses of BMN 351. In part two, the participants in Cohort 1A transitioned to once-weekly dosing. The participants in Cohort 1B, 2 and 3 will receive low (6 mg/kg), medium (9 mg/kg) and high (12 mg/kg) doses of BMN 351 and continue once-weekly dosing at that same dose.
For more information, please visit clinicaltrials.biomarin.com .
About Late-Onset Pompe Disease
Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) is an inherited lysosomal disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA). Reduced or absent levels of GAA lead to accumulation of glycogen in cells, which is believed to result in the clinical manifestations of Pompe disease. LOPD can be severe and debilitating with progressive muscle weakness throughout the body that worsens over time, particularly in skeletal muscles and muscles that control breathing.
About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe neuromuscular condition that leads to progressive muscle weakness and premature mortality. DMD is caused by genetic changes that result in the absence or dysfunction of dystrophin, an essential protein that is necessary for preserving muscle function.
As an X-linked disorder, DMD primarily affects young boys, with onset of symptoms occurring around 2 to 3 years of age. The incidence of DMD is up to 1 in 3,600 to 6,000 live male births.
Individuals with DMD experience serious functional impairments, including loss of limb strength and ambulation, and respiratory and cardiovascular impacts that require lifelong care.
POMBILITI + OPFOLDA is a two-component therapy that consists of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga, a bis-M6P-enriched rhGAA that facilitates high-affinity uptake through the M6P receptor while retaining its capacity for processing into the most active form of the enzyme, and the oral enzyme stabilizer

articles.title_orig: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.title_zh: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.content_orig:
Saturn is at its biggest and brightest as the ringed planet reaches opposition this weekend.
Opposition happens as Earth passes between Saturn and the Sun, bringing the planet to its closest point to Earth for the year, about 784 million miles (1.26 billion km) away. This minimum distance makes Saturn appear brighter than at any other time this year.
Opposition is a great time to observe Saturn because it rises in the east around sunset, reaches its highest point around midnight, and remains visible through dawn. It will appear as a yellowish point of light in the eastern and southeastern sky.
You do not need a telescope to see Saturn, but even a small telescope can reveal the planet's rings and the brightest couple of its 293 moons. While you are spotting Saturn, look a bit higher for a large grouping of four stars astronomers call the Great Square of Pegasus. Up and to the right is the Circlet (ring) of Pisces. These are asterisms, or recognizable patterns within the more official constellations of Pegasus (the winged horse) and Pisces (the fish).
2026's view is very different from last year's when Earth crossed the plane of Saturn’s rings. Though the ring system spans about 175,000 miles, it is, on average, about 30 feet thick, so it effectively disappears when viewed edge-on. Since opposition in 2025, the rings are tilted 7.5 degrees from our perspective, bringing them back into view.
Saturn will be at opposition on Sunday morning at 8:21 a.m., but with clouds expected this weekend, the best views will be tonight, Friday, Oct. 2. The planet will remain an excellent evening target for much of the month.
Saturn’s last opposition occurred Sept. 21, 2025. Saturn reaches opposition every 378 days, or about two weeks later each year, as Earth catches up with Saturn in its orbit. We'll have similar good opportunities to view Jupiter as it reaches its own opposition on Feb. 11, 2027, followed by Mars on Feb. 19, 2027.

articles.title_orig: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.title_zh: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › People News
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has announced that Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett will serve as co-directors starting next year, while Rima Dael will conclude her service as CEO.
Mead, NFCB’s director of member engagement, and Aston-Puckett, its chief operating officer, bring around four decades of combined nonprofit and community media experience, including work at KZMU(FM) in Utah and KVNF(FM) in Colorado.
The change is effective Jan. 1. With the move, Rima Dael will conclude her service as the organization’s CEO at the end of December as the association moves to a two-person permanent staff. The nonprofit has a nine-person board of directors.
[Related: “Future in Focus: Rima Dael of the NFCB”]
Dael supported the structural change and is helping lead the transition, according to NFCB. She has not accepted another position. The organization’s board credited Dael’s leadership in strengthening fundraising, research, partnerships and national advocacy.
According to a release, the change follows board and staff planning in response to the loss of Corporation for Public Broadcasting support. NFCB said it is aligning its expenses with membership revenue while keeping assistance, training, regulatory guidance, resources and peer connections as its focus.
NFCB received a $1.25 million general operating grant from the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation in 2025. It is investing in member resources including rural audience research, an updated legal handbook, emergency preparedness tools and station training.
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has been serving the nation’s community radio stations since 1978.
